svg.text: Eight reflective IR channels with a shared pulsed LED bus, read differentially by the Teensy 4.1.
J-S3 … J-S8 — each channel populated identically:
1 kΩ, 4.7 kΩ and 220 Ω each, as channel 1
TO-220 from the front: G – D – S
Installed in the machine: own regulator on the board, fed with 5 V through J-PWR.
keep together — 100 nF adjacent to U1 pins 2/3, electrolytics as short as possible
Identically named symbols are connected: all 3.3 V together, all GND together, all LED BUS together.
VARIANT B — supplied from the Teensy (prototype / breadboard)
Supplied from the Teensy’s 3V3 pin, no regulator. The channel section above is unchanged.
Both in parallel, not in series.
At the 3.3 V entry, leads short.
Budget: 87.6 mA worst case from the 3V3 pin, against ≈ 250 mA available.
No fault isolation — a short on the
sensor cable hits the regulator inside the Teensy.
B ends when A is built: populate U1, its capacitors
and J-PWR, move the 3.3 V feed, re-terminate J-T.
C5 and C6 sit on the 3.3 V rail in variant A too.
HT7333-A TO-92 pin order: 1 = GND, 2 = IN, 3 = OUT — not the 7805 or LD1117 order.
C2 at U1 pin 2, C4 at U1 pin 3
shortest path for the high-frequency current
C1 at U1 pin 2, C3 at U1 pin 3
output capacitor is in the LDO control loop
1 kΩ gate resistor, 100 kΩ pull-down at Q1 gate
gate loop pickup, defined gate at boot
C5 and C6 at the 3.3 V entry, both variants
filters what arrives, where it arrives
The HT73xx-A datasheet states no placement distance, so none is claimed here. What matters is which parts belong together, listed above.
